correctness.rationale: Every permutation-invariant code is a union of weight layers. Domination yields all consecutive-triple conditions. Distinct unit vectors (and complementary pairs) force the two boundary pairs. Separation of all pairs follows by exact Hamming-distance cases 1, 2, or >=3, with nonshared intermediate neighbors n-2>0 for unequal-weight distance-two pairs. The 4-state DP enumerates precisely all legal layer profiles with binomial costs. Central binomial concentration gives lower limiting density >=1/3, while residue mod 3 layer constructions attain <=2^n/3+8/3. Two different exact algorithms verify n=3..14 outcomes, with direct entire-cube signature tests through n=7. No computation is used to infer the infinite result.

value.rationale: Demanding interchangeable coordinate positions is a natural deployment symmetry in Hamming fault-diagnosis networks. The new characterization avoids exponentially large signature constraints, converting optimal symmetric sensing into a four-state exact algorithm. Its limiting one-third fraction gives a genuine structural cost compared with unrestricted code constructions. The result is all-dimensional and not a routine fixed graph enumeration, with exact small-n checks and explicit natural limits.
